subject: CardinalPay: sudden p95/p99 spike on Hosted API - recovery plan and exec summary
message_1_subject: Re: API latency spike this morning (p95/p99)
message_1_body:
Hi Irene —

This morning at ~08:06 UTC we saw a large spike in inference latency for calls routed to your hosted API. p95 jumped from ~170ms to ~1.9s and p99 to ~3.5–4s for about 18 minutes; ~2% of requests returned 503s. Attached are the client-side traces and an aggregated log window (cardinal_logs_20280615.txt).

We are live with our scheduled payment batch at 08:00 and this burst correlates with that job; we only started seeing it after you rolled the autoscaler changes last weekend. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your end that would affect cold-start behavior or routing? This is impacting live transactions so we need a mitigation ASAP.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Director, Platform Reliability
CardinalPay

---

message_2_subject: Re: API latency spike this morning (p95/p99)
message_2_body:
Hi Alicia — thanks for the data and sorry for the disruption. I’m escalating this to SRE/Eng and copying Marissa for account coordination.

Quick notes from my side: we shipped an autoscaler tuning PR (reduce-min-warm->0 for aggressive cost savings) last Saturday that may have increased downtime between scale events for low steady traffic tenants. We are treating this as a priority.

Immediate asks: can you confirm the request pattern for 08:00–08:20 (QPS, payload sizes) and whether you were pinned to any specific model variant? I’ll open an internal incident and propose a short mitigation: (1) pin your routing to a warmed pool variant or (2) temporarily raise min_warm_instances for your pool while we triage. Marissa will coordinate credits and a follow-up call.

I’ve opened ticket RED-4281 and attached the initial telemetry link.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/cardinalpay/dash/7Xw2k
message_3_subject: RE: API latency spike this morning (p95/p99) — initial triage
message_3_body:
I did a first-pass triage on RED-4281. Summary: around 08:05–08:12 we saw a burst that caused rapid scale-outs. New GPU instances were being provisioned and completed the handshake ~28–34s after the first allocation; cold-start path (container + model init + kernel selection) contributed the majority of p95/p99 regressions. The autoscaler had aggressively downscaled idle capacity overnight (min_warm_instances was 0 for several tenant pools).

Key timestamps and metrics:
- 08:06:12 UTC: QPS spike to ~240 (baseline ~40)
- 08:07–08:10: instances allocated, first healthy at 08:07:45
- Observed p95 ~1.8s, p99 ~3.6s during ramp; after warmed instances served, p95 returned to ~180ms within ~9 minutes.

Short-term recommendations I’ve applied in prod for CardinalPay (rollback/measures):
1) Increased min_warm_instances for CardinalPay shard to 2 (emergency override).
2) Extended scale-down cooldown to keep warmed instances around during expected bursts.
3) Pinned routing for CardinalPay to the warmed replica set while we run a deeper kernel warm-up.

I’m attaching a triage screenshot of the allocation timeline. Longer-term: we need per-tenant warm reservations, better pre-warming heuristics tied to cron-like schedules (customer batch windows), and monitoring alerts that tie p99 regressions to scale events.

— Rishi
(Engineering — Serving Runtime)
Attachment: triage-screenshot.png
message_4_subject: CardinalPay — immediate mitigation and next steps
message_4_body:
Hi Alicia — I’m really sorry for the impact this morning. We’ve put an emergency mitigation in place (Irene and Rishi’s team) and are monitoring metrics.

What we’ve done for you now:
- Increased reserved warm capacity for your pool for the next 24 hours.
- Temporarily routed production traffic to warmed replicas to avoid further cold starts.
- We will issue a partial service credit for this window; I’ll follow up with the exact amount after we finish the postmortem.

Next steps: schedule a 30-min call with our SRE and runtime engineering to review a permanent per-tenant warm reservation and Cron-based pre-warm (we propose a 1:00–1:30 UTC pre-warm for your daily batch). Please suggest a time.

Again — apologies and thank you for the quick data you sent.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
message_5_subject: RE: API latency spike this morning — emergency changes applied
message_5_body:
Update from SRE: emergency policy changes were applied at 09:35 UTC. Details: min_warm_instances for CardinalPay set to 2, scale-down window extended to 300s for that shard, and we force-warmed the KV cache on the two new instances (preloaded recent prefixes).

Observed effect: within ~8 minutes after the change p95 dropped to ~220ms and p99 to ~820ms for the routed traffic window. Error rate from 2% down to below 0.1%. We’re keeping extra telemetry retention on RED-4281 for 72 hours.

I will capture the exact diff (warm-pool-change.patch.diff) and post to the incident.

— Hannah
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

message_6_subject: Exec summary: CardinalPay cold-start spike, mitigation, and proposed fixes
message_6_body:
Evelyn —

Brief executive summary and asks following yesterday’s CardinalPay incident (RED-4281).

What happened:
- On 2028-06-15 08:06 UTC a scheduled payment batch from CardinalPay caused a sudden burst. Due to a recent autoscaler tuning (min_warm_instances defaulted aggressively to 0 for cost savings), we experienced scale-outs that relied on cold-start paths. Cold-start latency (container load + model init + kernel selection) drove p95/p99 regressions and a small spike in 503s.

Immediate impact & mitigation:
- Impact window ~08:06–08:24 UTC, peak p99 ~3.6s, error rate ~2% at peak.
- SRE/Eng applied emergency overrides (min_warm_instances=2, extended cooldown, pinned routing) and observed p95/p99 return to baseline within ~10 minutes.
- We informed the customer, routed traffic to warmed replicas, and offered a credit.

Root-cause hypothesis:
1) Aggressive downscale default combined with tenant workloads that have predictable cron bursts.
2) Kernel-selection path and the quantized variant we rolled last quarter has a longer first-inference setup time on newer hardware/driver combos.

Proposed short-to-medium term actions (ask: approval to proceed):
- Roll back the autoscaler PR that set min_warm_instances default to 0; instead set a conservative default of 1 and allow per-tenant override (Ops approval required).
- Build per-tenant warm reservation feature (priority-high) and a Cron-based pre-warm scheduler for recurring batch windows (engineering sprint request).
- Add an alert that correlates p99 regressions with scale events.
- Postmortem and customer-facing RCA by EOD Friday; proposed 10% service credit for the impacted window.

We estimate the near-term cost impact of keeping small warm reservations for high-burst tenants at ~0.7% incremental infra spend but believe this materially reduces outage risk for high-revenue customers.

Please reply with approval to proceed on the rollback + per-tenant warm reservation build. If you prefer, I can route this to the Exec Ops meeting later today.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
